svg.aria-label: How to write શહેર: 4 parts, શ, હ, ે, ર, one after another
svg.title: Writing શહેર
svg.desc: 4 parts written one after another: શ, હ, ે, ર (gujarati). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which in Gujarati is the order they are typed: each sign comes after its consonant, even the i sign, which sits to the left of it. Each sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: શ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, શ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; હ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, હ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ે: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/6_ke.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the e sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; ર: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ર animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source notes on variation: શ: The teaching app animates શ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper right, circles the small upper loop, then continues through the broad lower body and into its lower-right tail. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate tall right spine before turning through the lower-right foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the small upper loop, broad lower body, tail, tall spine, and lower foot, but its printed body is wider and more angular and its spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's loop-and-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loop, body, tail, spine, foot, and terminals differently. હ: The teaching app animates હ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper right, circles the compact upper loop, threads through the middle turn, then continues around the broad lower bowl into its rightward finish without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the compact upper loop, middle turn, broad lower bowl, and rightward finish, but its printed form separates the upper and lower contours and makes the turns wider and more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path fits each run to the font's ink and uses a short connecting bridge between those disconnected printed contours to preserve the source's upper-loop-to-middle-turn-to-lower-bowl order and zero-lift evidence. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loop, turn, bowl, finish, and terminals differently. ે: In the template for કે, and in all 33 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ે is one pen-down run that starts at the upper-left tip, arcs right and comes down to the lower right, where it meets the consonant. t30apps, already cited for એ, sweeps the matching high arc from left to right, last. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 162 of its 165 stored prototypes of the e sign (98%) are one stroke, most running from the upper left down to the lower right. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. ર: The teaching app animates ર as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper left, circles clockwise around the rounded upper body, narrows through the middle, curls around the small middle loop, then descends diagonally into the lower-right tail without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the rounded upper body, narrow middle, small loop, and descending tail, but its printed turns are wider and more angular and its tail broader than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-body-to-middle-loop-to-lower-tail order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the body, loop, tail, and terminals differently.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 parts, one after another
Part 3 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Part 1: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, શ animation, first and second SVG paths
Part 2: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, હ animation, first SVG path
Part 3: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/6_ke.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the e
Part 4: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ર animation, first SVG path
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
